pr_title: Avoid truncating/breaking some Type3 glyphs in `compileType3Glyph` (bug 1245391, issue 10568)
pr_body:
*Hopefully this patch makes sense, since I cannot claim to fully understand this function.*

With the changes made in PR #3354 *some* Type3 glyph outlines are no longer rendering correctly, since the final paths were being accidentally ignored.
The fact that Type3 fonts are not very common in PDF documents, and that most Type3 glyphs are unaffected by this regression, probably explains why this has gone unnoticed since 2013.

Fixes [bug 1245391](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1245391)
Fixes #10568

issue_context.title: "ほ" is displayed like "は"
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:

[sample01.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/2884257/sample01.pdf)

[sample02.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/2884258/sample02.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version:
FireFox 65.0.1 64bit
- Operating system and its version:
Windows 10 ver 1803
- PDF.js version:
2.1.97
- Is a browser extension:
No

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Open sample1.pdf or sample2.pdf by FireFox.

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)

"ほ" want to be displayed as the ruby of "保" in sample1.pdf.
"ほう" want to be displayed as the ruby of "報" in sample2.pdf.

What went wrong? (add screenshot)

"は" is displayed as the ruby of "保" in sample1.pdf.
"はう" is displayed as the ruby of "報" in sample2.pdf.

![sample1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47815682/53086691-ef498100-3548-11e9-8b8c-ed9e9476f945.png)

![sample2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47815682/53086712-f8d2e900-3548-11e9-8b6b-4c83aec20015.png)

The images displayed by Edge (17.17134) on the left and FireFox (65.0.1) on the right.

Link to a viewer (if hosted on a site other than mozilla.github.io/pdf.js or as Firefox/Chrome extension):
comments: This is a Type3 font issue which looks *very* similar to [bug 1245391](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1245391), please note https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1245391#c6 in particular.
This *may* be a regression from PR #3354, @fkaelberer would you be able to take a look?

@Snuffleupagus 
Thanks a lot, for your information!

I modified PDF.js used in our project to set false to COMPILE_TYPE3_GLYPHS,
then "ほ" is now displayed as "ほ".

We are going to check a lot of PDF files from now on to see if other characters have not changed.

Thanks again.

review_comments: removing this is not preferable: could you try to move `--count` after `points[p]` is set to 0. you can see that at line 323 it may or may not do that, so in the else branch let's add the check `if (!points[p]) --count;`

Sure, let's see how this works out on the bots :-)

(If it turns out to be more complicated, someone who actually understands this code will have to take over fixing the bug though.)
It seems that this worked out just fine; does this mean that the patch is good to go now?
